string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of China and an important center for politics, culture, international communication, science and technology. It is both an ancient capital and a modern international city. Historic landmarks include the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, the Summer Palace and sections of the Great Wall. These places reflect different aspects of imperial history, architecture and cultural traditions. Alongside its historic buildings, Beijing supports scientific research, technological innovation and cultural exchange. Visitors can explore its museums and heritage sites to understand how the city connects its long history with modern development.

Shanghai is a municipality directly under the central government in eastern China. Located at the mouth of the Yangtze River, it forms part of the Yangtze River Delta. The city plays a major role in international finance, trade and shipping. Its port connects regional industries with global markets and handles large volumes of container traffic. Shanghai is also an important center for scientific research and technological innovation. The city continues to develop its economy through international connections, modern services and research activities. Its coastal location helps explain its strong role in commerce and transportation.

Chongqing is a municipality directly under the central government in southwestern China. It lies along the upper reaches of the Yangtze River, and its central urban area is located where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet. Mountains, hills, valleys and rivers give the region a distinctive landscape. Its varied terrain has shaped the arrangement of urban districts and surrounding settlements. The municipality includes major urban areas as well as agricultural and rural communities. River networks, mountain scenery and karst landforms are important features of the wider region, explaining its familiar identity as a mountain city.

Tianjin is a municipality directly under the central government in northern China. It lies near Beijing and faces the Bohai Sea, giving it an important position in regional transportation and trade. Tianjin Port connects northern inland areas with international shipping networks. The city developed into a major center of modern industry, commerce and education. Binhai New Area supports economic development and opening to international business. Tianjin also takes part in coordinated development with Beijing and Hebei. Its coastal location and transport connections make it an important gateway for northern China.
